audience: DRAFT — inferred from the case studies and blog, please correct: founders, product and marketing leads, and agency partners (e.g. the Dentsu Webchutney work) deciding who to build with; designers and developers reading the blog.
doList: Write in the first person (we, or I in a byline post) and say what was actually done.
Use numbers and named tools where you have them.
dontList: Open with the market ("In today's fast-paced digital landscape…").
Announce the article ("In this blog, we will explore…").
Stack adjectives in place of a claim (seamless, cutting-edge, world-class).
persona: A product and experience architecture studio that works across strategy, brand, experience, engineering, growth and operations — one team, six disciplines. At its best the writing is plain, specific and first-hand: it says what was built and why, admits the trade-off, and names the tool or the number. That is how the About intro and the founder's recent posts read; the older blog and service copy does not.
sampleBad: In today's fast-paced digital landscape, branding has become more crucial than ever for businesses to create a lasting impression and stand out from the competition.
Resonant brand foundations are architected through the synthesis of strategic insight and creative brilliance, driving measurable business growth.
sampleGood: A product and experience architecture studio. We work across strategy, brand, experience, engineering, growth and operations — one team, six disciplines, and a single view of the thing being built.
We start focused, prove value early, and scale what works.
Supabase is the right call for most projects. Here's when NoSQL wins instead: evolving schemas, deep relationships, cheap MVP scaling and real-time sync.
seoDescription: Wugweb is a digital experience agency crafting brand strategy, UX design, martech, AI, and web development for ambitious teams.
writingPrinciples: Lead with the claim, then the evidence.
Name the specifics — the tool, the number, the constraint — instead of an adjective.
Say who does what. Active voice: "We start focused, prove value early, and scale what works."
Admit the trade-off; it is what makes the recommendation believable.
Cut the throat-clearing. Start with the point, not the market.
